items.title: How much more does the same bug cost to fix, the later it's caught?
items.description: Aegis's string-concatenated SQL bug cost about 10 minutes of a developer's time because SAST caught it in the same pull request it was written in. Vantage's identical bug reached production and cost a full incident response, customer notification, and remediation. This is a well-documented industry pattern, not a coincidence: fixing a defect costs roughly an order of magnitude more at each stage it survives past — commit, build, staging, a pentest, and finally production. Drag the number of stages the bug survives to see the same starting cost compound.

params.name: baseFixCost
params.label: Cost to fix at commit time (SAST catches it immediately)

params.name: stagesSurvived
params.label: Stages the bug survives before being caught

items.compute: const stageNames = ['Commit (SAST)', 'Build (SCA)', 'Staging (DAST)', 'Pentest', 'Production incident']; const cost = Math.round(params.baseFixCost * Math.pow(10, params.stagesSurvived)); return { fixCost: cost };

outputs.label: Cost to fix the same bug
